applies_why: The judge treats Matthew 1:16 as UNDERDETERMINED because its wording admits two readings, which the rule addresses.
quote: UNDERDETERMINED -- the passive egennēthē (was born) with feminine hēs (of whom) admits both the withheld-father and the birth-narration readings
rule_words: That a single verse does not state a link or its contrary is never a ground for STANDS or UNDERDETERMINED, for either side. A verse that carries two senses at once is not open. Both senses stand.
room: "A verse that carries two senses at once is not open. Both senses stand." I weighed (a) a verse admitting two senses is open/UNDERDETERMINED, against (b) such a verse is not open and both senses stand.
why: The judge’s stated ground for UNDERDETERMINED is that the verse admits both readings, which K-S2 forbids treating as open.
